name: Orangey Brown
lede: Orangey Brown is a deep, rust-toned brown named by plain grammar: the modifier "orangey" pushing the base color [[brown]] toward orange.

sections.title: A modifier on an existing color
sections.body:
*Orangey* softens [[orange]] into a qualifier rather than a color on its own, the same pattern seen in [[scarlet|Orangey Red]]; paired with *brown*, it marks this as a brown pulled toward orange rather than a new name in its own right [1]. The exact value comes from the 2010 xkcd online color-name survey, and nothing in our sources records who first used the two-word phrase; it reads as ordinary English, not a coined name [1].

The nearest named look-alike on file is [[brown-orange|Brown Orange]], almost the same shade from the opposite word order [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A close match to this brown appears in 286 of our 23,781 archived paintings, about 1.2 per cent, with the within-painting lens finding it in 156; more common than 67 per cent of our named colors [3]. It most often plays an accent, and Adriaen van Ostade is its most devoted painter here, carrying it in 4 of his 39 archived works [3]. The earliest dated match, from 1240, sits 770 years before the 2010 survey name; that gap is a floor, not a first sighting, as photographed, not a pigment test [3].
